title: Yukon Home Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps up to $24,000, Windows, Insulation
desc: Yukon home rebates for 2026: 100% of a heat pump up to $24,000 for lower incomes, 50% up to $10,500 for everyone, plus insulation up to $12,000 and window rebates. Every amount sourced.
sub: A plain guide to Yukon's 2026 Good Energy rebates and the Dependable Grid Program. Each amount comes from the Government of Yukon's own pages, read on October 21, 2026.
sections: The Government of Yukon runs the Good Energy rebates for homes, with some funding from the federal Low Carbon Economy Fund. A newer set, the Dependable Grid Program, started in 2026 to cut winter electricity demand. The Energy Branch answers questions at energy@yukon.ca or 867-393-7063, toll-free in the Yukon at 1-800-661-0408. Its office is on the 2nd floor of 4114 4th Avenue, RBC Building, Whitehorse, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. Our Yukon rebate calculator adds up only what is open for your home.

Affordable Heat Pump Program. For lower-income households, this covers 100% of a heat pump project up to $24,000, including electrical upgrades and controls. You must own the home, live in it, and have it be at least 6 months old. You must be approved before installing: anything installed first is not eligible. Your after-tax household income (line 23600 minus line 43500 for every adult) must be under:

ResidentsAfter-tax income limit
1$53,820
2$110,400
3$139,150
4$163,300
5 or more$184,000

Households that heat with oil get a $250 upfront payment from Natural Resources Canada. You cannot use the program if you received funding from NRCan's Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program.

Heat pump rebate. Everyone else, and anyone not approved, can claim 50% of project costs up to $10,500 for an air-source heat pump on NRCan's cold climate list for Manitoba and Yukon, or an ENERGY STAR ground-source heat pump. Keep your existing heat as a backup. Electric-heated homes must also enrol in Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home program. Cheques come within 12 weeks.

Ottawa announced a National Heat Pump Rebate on October 8, 2026, expected to start in early 2027. How it will combine with Yukon programs is not published yet. See our National Heat Pump Rebate guide.

You need an energy assessment before insulation or air sealing rebates, and another after the work. The home must be 5 years or older. Maximums:

  • Above-ground walls: up to $12,000, and you must at least double the existing insulation level. The amount follows the share of wall area you insulate.
  • Below-ground walls: up to $10,000, in proportion to depth up to 6 feet.
  • Slab or floor system: $2,000.
  • Attic: $2,500, for an attic at R40 or less raised to R60 or more.
  • Air sealing: $5,000 per building when you reach 1.5 air changes per hour or fewer, with an HRV installed.

ENERGY STAR windows pay $120 each, up to $1,800 per home, for complete window assemblies in a heated building at least five years old.

For homes with electric heat, the Dependable Grid Program pays 50% of costs for new heating that lowers winter electricity use:

  • Primary oil or propane heating: up to $15,000 for existing homes.
  • Secondary oil, propane or wood backup: up to $5,000.
  • Dual fuel, a heat pump plus a non-electric backup that works in a power outage: up to $15,000.

You do not need to remove your electric heating. Wood heating systems, such as EPA-listed stoves, boilers and pellet stoves, also earn 50% up to $2,500 in buildings 5 years or older.
Financing and what we did not read

The Better Buildings program offers low-cost funding of up to 25% of the property's assessed value, to a maximum of $50,000, repaid through a local improvement tax. Yukon's rebate page also lists rebates for heat recovery ventilators, drain-water heat recovery, ENERGY STAR appliances, solar hot water, smart thermostats and hot water tank controllers, and new homes. We did not read those pages, so we do not list their amounts.
faq: How much is the Yukon heat pump rebate?
50% of project costs up to $10,500. Lower-income households can instead apply to the Affordable Heat Pump Program for 100% up to $24,000 if approved before installation.
What is the income limit for the Affordable Heat Pump Program?
After-tax household income under $53,820 for 1 resident, $110,400 for 2, $139,150 for 3, $163,300 for 4 and $184,000 for 5 or more.
Do I need to get approval before installing?
For the Affordable Heat Pump Program, yes. Installations before approval are not eligible, though you can still apply for the 50% heat pump rebate.
How much does Yukon pay for windows?
$120 per ENERGY STAR window, up to $1,800 per home or building at least five years old.
What is the Dependable Grid Program?

A 2026 program that pays 50% of costs for non-electric heating in electric-heated homes: up to $15,000 for a primary system, $5,000 for a backup, and $15,000 for a heat pump plus a non-electric backup.
